item.title: The Rams’ season starts now
item.description: The Los Angeles Rams dug themselves out of a 2-4 hole en route to 6-4. They put together a four-game win streak. On the surface it seems like their early season struggles have all been corrected. In reality, their last four opponents have a combined record of 11-26-1. Cardinals 3-7 Chargers: 1-8 Commanders: 3-5-1 Raiders: 4-6 It’s reasonable to look at the last month’s schedule and conclude we really learned nothing about the Rams. Of course, they should be given credit for keeping losing teams losing. Who are the Rams following their recent rash of injuries? What happens when stiffer competition slows LA’s run game and they must rely on an inconsistent and short-handed passing attack? The defense has stymied offenses of late. What happens when they face the likes of Jordan Love, Patrick Mahomes, Brock Purdy, and Dak Prescott in the coming weeks? One thing is still true: the Rams have three lives left in the NFC playoff picture It will take 10 wins to make the playoffs. In other words, they cannot take more than three losses moving forward without leaving their destiny up to factors outside of their control. When looking on the horizon, LA’s season effectively starts out of their bye week. Week 11: BYE Week 12: vs Green Bay Packers Perhaps the single-most important game left. The Rams are competing directly with NFC West teams in the race for their own division, although the 49ers may be running away with it. They are also indirectly competing against the NFC North . This Wednesday night game is the perfect opportunity to ding Green Bay and bolster their own chances. It carries significant playoff weight. Week 13: vs Kansas City Chiefs Unimportant in terms of the NFC tiebreakers, although the Rams really cannot afford to use one of their remaining three lives this early. Week 14: at San Francisco 49ers Can LA avenge their Week 1 loss where they looked enitely unprepared to play. Week 15: vs Dallas Cowboys Dallas can light up the scoreboard. It will be a tough test for the defense. The offense may need more production than simply grounding the game out on the ground in order to keep pace. Week 16: at Seattle Seahawks It’s tough closing the season out with the Seahawks in two of the final three weeks. The silver lining is that winning both matchups would effectively eliminate Seattle and reinforce LA’s destiny. They must take care of business or they could be left on the outside looking in. The deal sends a clear message that the South Siders are willing to splash the cash to get their rotation depth intact ahead of 2027, but it also means that the move could backfire should things not go well. The White Sox giving May $17.5 million annually is a bold financial commitment from a franchise that has historically avoided multi-year contracts to starting pitchers, whose career has been a rollercoaster of injuries and a struggle to reach full potential. So, he has useful experience, one that no pitcher in the White Sox clubhouse has. But the big question is what version of May will take the mound at Rate Field. item.title: Spurs fashion: Wemby rocks Supreme, Vassell goes luxury, McLaughlin shows soccer love
item.description: Victor Wembanyama wears a Supreme x Nike jacket, Supreme beanie and light-wash jeans ahead of Tuesday's game against the Detroit Pistons. (Courtesy of the San Antonio Spurs) The San Antonio Spurs brought a little bit of everything to the pregame fashion tunnel Tuesday night: a French superstar rocking Supreme, a guard making sweater weather look expensive and another possibly revealing his soccer allegiance. Ahead of their 7 p.m. matchup against the Detroit Pistons at the Frost Bank Center, Victor Wembanyama, Devin Vassell and Jordan McLaughlin turned heads with looks featuring Nike collaborations, Balenciaga denim and a nod to Manchester City superstar Erling Haaland. Here's what the Spurs wore before hitting the hardwood. Victor Wembanyama Wembanyama kept things casual, arriving in a black Supreme x Nike Nylon Hooded Jacket paired with a Supreme beanie, light-wash jeans and Nike sneakers. The 7-foot-4 French superstar opted for a relaxed streetwear look, trading some of his more adventurous fashion choices for a simple outfit featuring two of the biggest names in streetwear and sportswear. Devin Vassell Vassell looked ready for sweater weather, but his outfit was anything but basic. The Spurs guard arrived wearing a camel-colored knitted Ralph Lauren sweater paired with Balenciaga Winter 22 Rhinestone Scribble Baggy Denim jeans, adding some sparkle to his cozy look. He accessorized with glasses and Apple over-ear headphones, keeping things stylish from head to nearly toe. His footwear wasn't visible, leaving one expensive mystery unanswered. Given Vassell's history of rocking luxury shoes, it wouldn't be surprising if another pricey pair completed his outfit. Jordan McLaughlin McLaughlin may have given Spurs fans a hint about his soccer allegiance with his latest pregame outfit. The Spurs guard rocked a Travis Scott Cactus Jack x Nike Athletes Series Haaland Hoodie, a collaboration featuring Manchester City striker Erling Haaland. Whether McLaughlin is a Manchester City supporter, a Haaland fan or simply likes the hoodie remains unclear, but his outfit certainly gave a nod to one of soccer's biggest stars. McLaughlin completed his look with a snapback cap and Air Jordan 1 "Top 3" sneakers, combining soccer-inspired fashion with classic basketball footwear. From Wembanyama's Supreme streetwear to Vassell's designer denim and McLaughlin's soccer-inspired hoodie, the Spurs once again showed that their individual styles extend well beyond the basketball court. item.title: Michigan State injury report: QB Milivojevic out; 7 questionable
item.description: Michigan State could be down to a true freshman quarterback once again when Oregon comes to Spartan Stadium this week. Starting quarterback Alessio Milivojevic is listed as out for Michigan State against No. 14 Oregon on the availability report released by the Big Ten on Nov. 17. Backup quarterback Cam Fancher is listed questionable. Updates to the report are due the next two days before a final report two hours before Friday's 8 p.m. kickoff. Michigan State (3-7, 1-6 Big Ten) is a 14 1/2-point underdog to Oregon (7-3, 5-2), which ESPN Analytics gives an 86.4 percent chance to win. In total, 10 Michigan State players are listed out, and seven are listed questionable, which is an improvement from 12 players listed out a week ago. Among those listed out are safety Devin Vaught, linebacker Jordan Hall, tight end Jayden Savoury, and defensive tackle Ben Roberts, the latter who reaggravated a knee injury after two snaps against Washington in a 21-14 loss Nov. 14. For Oregon, outside linebacker Teitum Tuioti is among eight players listed out. Inside linebacker Jerry Mixon is questionable, while defensive lineman Bear Alexander is probable. Also out for the Ducks remains Detroit King alumnus Dante Moore, who has not played since being hit while going down for a slide in a Sept. 26 win over Southern Cal. Milivojevic (left arm) will miss his second game of the season. He was unavailable for an Oct. 24 loss to UCLA at the Rose Bowl, where true freshman Kayd Coffman made his first career start. The East Kentwood product might start again if Fancher (right knee) cannot play. Coffman threw completions on his first four passes including a touchdown, but has since thrown seven incompletions including an interception including one throw on a three-and-out against Washington. Alongside Fancher, wide receiver Rodney Bullard Jr., running back Jaziun Patterson, cornerback Tre Bell, nickelback Michael Richard, left guard Conner Moore and tight end Brennan Parachek are listed questionable. Bell was a game-time decision against Washington but did not play. Moore injured his right knee one snap before Milivojevic's injury, while Richard went down in the second half and did not return. The story of Michigan State’s football season could be told through its injury report. Its best summary is the data: Out of 42 players to start at least one game, 13 of them are out or questionable accounting for a combined 80 starts out of 220 as a team. On offense, Michigan State is missing 1,559 snaps, 20 percent of its season total. On defense, 2,657 missing snaps account for a loss of 40 percent. cearegood@detroitnews.com @ConnorEaregood This article originally appeared on The Detroit News: Michigan State injury report: QB Milivojevic out; 7 questionable

item.title: Álex Baena now leads Atlético’s attack, but he needs more help
item.description: MADRID, SPAIN - NOVEMBER 15: Alex Baena and Marc Cucurella of Spain walk out with teammates for the second half during the UEFA Nations League 2026/27 group phase match between Spain and England at Riyadh Air Metropolitano on November 15, 2026 in Madrid, Spain. (Photo by David Ramos - UEFA/UEFA via Getty Images) | UEFA via Getty Images When Atlético signed Álex Baena from Villarreal, the expectation was creativity, not goals. Twelve league games into this season, he is the club’s top scorer with five, ahead of Julián Alvarez, Alexander Sørloth and Jonathan David. It is tempting to call it a hot streak. The evidence points to something more lasting: a player whose confidence changed over one summer, in a team that has learned to share its goals around. A summer that changed everything Baena’s first year at the Metropolitano was not easy. Spanish coverage at the time described a slow adaptation to Diego Simeone’s demands, with flashes of quality but little end product. Then came the World Cup. Baena was one of three Atlético players in Spain’s winning squad, alongside Marcos Llorente and Marc Pubill, and the only one of them to start the final against Argentina. He played 75 minutes at MetLife Stadium before Nico Williams replaced him, and Williams went on to set up the winning goal. The change since August has been visible. Baena scored a sumptuous free kick in round one against Málaga, then scored twice in the 3-1 win at Sevilla in August. He has kept his production since. Five goals and three assists in 12 league games mean he has had a hand in eight of Atlético’s 23 goals, more than a third. Goals from everywhere The more interesting story is what Baena’s rise says about the team. Atlético have scored 23 league goals, and they come from all over the pitch. Player League goals Matches Álex Baena 5 12 Giuliano Simeone 4 12 Alejandro Grimaldo 4 11 Jonathan David 3 7 Lee Kang-in 2 12 Four players already have three goals or more, and a left-back, Álex Grimaldo, sits joint second. That is the opposite of Real Madrid, where Mbappé has 13 of 31 goals . Atlético’s top scorer accounts for just 22% of the team’s goals. For a Simeone side, that balance is a strength. It makes Atlético harder to plan for, and it suits a team that has conceded only 10 goals, joint-best in La Liga. It is also why the experts at TelecomAsia see Atlético as a genuine top-three side rather than a team waiting for one striker to fire. The Alvarez question None of this means Atlético can do without Alvarez. Last season he scored 20 goals and added nine assists in 49 matches. This season he returned to action he spent the summer publicly pushing for a move to Barcelona, and the slow start showed. The tone has since changed. Álvarez apologised to Atlético supporters , calling the episode a mistake, and last month he scored in consecutive games for the first time this season. He is under contract until 2030. The Baltimore Ravens have experienced their share of heartbreaking losses over the years, but the latest one has some people worried about the long-term identity of the franchise. Assuming Lamar Jackson signs an extension like many anticipate, the superstar quarterback will continue to be a focal point when on the field. However, this organization has obstacles to maneuver beyond just his injury status and contract situation. Ravens offensive coordinator Declan Doyle has a plan in mind, influenced in part from working under Ben Johnson on the Chicago Bears last season, but he may not have the pieces in place to execute that blueprint. “One of the things that’s shown since the Lamar injury is {Doyle} running kind of Chicago’s offense without Chicago’s personnel,” former quarterback and current NFL analyst Dan Orlovsky said on Tuesday’s edition of NFL Live. “They don’t have the blocking tight ends that certainly are needed to play in this offense. I don’t think their perimeter players block in this offense the way like Chicago’s do. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) “It’s certainly an across-the-board offensive issue that I do think is going to open the eyes {of management} after this season gets done. Adding to this offense not necessarily strictly talent, but the necessary skill set of people to run Declan Doyle’s offense, if he’s still the offensive coordinator there.” "It's certainly an across-the-board offensive issue." @danorlovsky7 weighs in on the Ravens' offense after their performance against the Chargers 👀 pic.twitter.com/OhkV8jAgy3 — NFL on ESPN (@ESPNNFL) November 17, 2026 Baltimore can only display so much offensive potency without Lamar Jackson, but the unit still has to perfect the little details in order to produce dynamic results. The offensive line is not meeting an acceptable standard, and its problems are magnified in No. 8’s absence. Despite scoring two touchdowns, Derrick Henry rushed 10 times for a shocking 10 yards in Monday’s brutal 23-20 home loss to the previously winless Los Angeles Chargers. The future Hall of Fame running back is now averaging only 3.8 yards per carry for the campaign. Even though Father Time is gaining, Doyle must figure out how to create more favorable opportunities for Henry and the rest of the offense. Yes, Jackson’s injury is going to cap the Ravens’ ceiling to an uncomfortably low level, and yes, Zay Flowers has to hold onto the ball in crucial moments, but there are still schematic and personnel-related issues the team must address. While it may be too late to affect meaningful change in 2026, Baltimore can still formulate its vision and begin to solidify player roles for 2027. item.title: South Africa coach Erasmus handed six-game ban for referee criticism
item.description: South Africa's Rassie Erasmus has been handed a six-game ban (FRANCK FIFE) South Africa coach Rassie Erasmus was handed a six-game ban by World Rugby on Tuesday for outspoken criticism of officials following a rare defeat for the world champions against France. Erasmus questioned the decision by the television match official not to intervene on a series of French tackles during his side's 21-19 loss in Paris. "If he didn't see it, it must be a technology problem. If he saw it and decided not to act on it, is that not match-fixing?" he said in a press conference in Dublin on Monday, ahead of the Springboks' clash against Ireland this weekend. The 54-year-old will be banned from "any match-day involvement" with his players and coaches and will not be allowed to even enter the stadium. "The panel determined that the conduct clearly amounts to disrespecting the authority of the match officials by impugning their integrity," World Rugby said in a statement. "Teams have access to well-established and supported channels and protocols for raising officiating matters before and after matches. "Challenging a decision is not the same as questioning an official's integrity or making comments that expose them to personal abuse." Erasmus is no stranger to disciplinary action for taking aim at officials. In 2021, he was banned from all rugby activity for two months by World Rugby for an hour-long video criticising the refereeing in the Springboks' first Test defeat by the British and Irish Lions. The following year, he received a two-match ban for a series of social media posts criticising officials in a defeat by France. South Africa Rugby has requested a full misconduct hearing. "The organisation respected the process but had requested an opportunity for its coach to contextualise his comments and assure the panel that it was not his intention to allege that any match official had acted with ulterior motives," said a spokesperson for SA Rugby. Erasmus could miss the final of the Nations Championship on November 29. South Africa trail New Zealand by one point at the top of the southern hemisphere standings with one round of fixtures to go. The other four matches are likely to be South Africa's opening fixtures of the 2027 Rugby Championship campaign, freeing Erasmus up to return in time for next year's World Cup in Australia. kca/lp

item.description: Argentina midfielder Nico Paz celebrates opening the scoring in his team's friendly thrashing of Costa Rica (Diego Lima) Rising star Nico Paz scored a superb double as Argentina bounced back from defeat with a 7-0 thrashing of Costa Rica in a friendly on Tuesday. Italy-based Como attacking midfielder Paz -- who has emerged as a reported transfer target for incoming Manchester United manager Mauricio Pochettino -- underscored his talent with two spectacular first-half goals in Cordoba. The 22-year-old, who scored twice in Como's 4-1 Champions League drubbing of United last month, lashed in Argentina's opener after just eight minutes at the Mario Alberto Kempes Stadium. After Atletico Madrid striker Julian Alvarez doubled Argentina's lead in the 35th minute, Paz then grabbed his second with the goal of the game. Picking up the ball in midfield, the young forward held off the attention of several Costa Rican markers before twisting and turning into space inside the penalty area and crashing a shot into the top corner to make it 3-0. Alvarez put Argentina into a 4-0 lead in the 43rd minute, beating Costa Rica goalkeeper Patrick Sequeira at the near post with a vicious shot that flew into the roof of the net. Paz's virtuoso first-half performance was the highlight of a one-sided encounter as Argentina bounced back from suffering a 2-1 defeat to Uruguay in Buenos Aires on Friday. Paz was substituted at half-time by Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni for Franco Mastantuono, the 19-year-old Fiorentina forward. Like Paz, Mastantuono is another member of Argentina's next generation of young talent as the former world champions rebuild following the retirement from international football of Lionel Messi. Mastantuono was quick to make his own mark on Tuesday's friendly, scoring just three minutes after coming on at half-time to make it 5-0. item.title: Toto Wolff reveals heartwarming memory of a teenage Kimi Antonelli living at his house
item.description: Motorsport photo The Formula 1 paddock is notoriously cutthroat, but Mercedes team principal Toto Wolff operates his driver management pipeline with a distinctly paternal approach. After guiding Kimi Antonelli from the junior karting ranks all the way to his historic 2026 world championship, Wolff recently shed light on just how deeply the 20-year-old is integrated into his actual family. In a recent exclusive interview with the German publication BILD , Wolff was asked to share his most beautiful personal memory of the young star. Rather than pointing to a specific race or a karting championship, Wolff recalled the time Antonelli spent living at his house in the United Kingdom. "Two or three years ago, he always slept at our house when he was at the factory in Brackley," Wolff explained. Because Antonelli was only 17 years old at the time and spending long, gruelling days working in the Mercedes simulator and engineering departments, Wolff felt a personal responsibility for his well-being. "He was still a minor, after all; we couldn't have just put him in a hotel," Wolff noted. "That's why he was practically a regular guest at Susie's and my [house]." Sleeping through the credits Living with the CEO of a multi-billion-dollar motorsport operation naturally led to some unique family downtime. Wolff shared that the trio would frequently sit down in the evenings to watch movies together to decompress from the factory work, but the viewing parties rarely went as planned. "In the evenings we often watched films together - although it was really just me," Wolff joked. Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes Andrea Kimi Antonelli, Mercedes, Toto Wolff, Mercedes According to Wolff, his wife, F1 Academy managing director Susie Wolff , is notorious for falling asleep within the first 10 minutes of a movie. Because Antonelli was also completely drained from his intense days working at the Brackley facility, the two would immediately pass out on the couch. "Then they both fell asleep shoulder to shoulder, and I watched the film alone," Wolff fondly recalled. Now, just a few short years after crashing on his boss's couch, Antonelli stands as the youngest drivers' world champion in F1 history - proving Wolff's personal, hands-on development strategy has paid off in full.
